channel.title: Tech Opinions Digest
channel.description: Daily tech opinions digest for Yun Zhou

item.title: Zvi Mowshowitz: AI #194 — Spy Versus Guy
item.description: Zvi's weekly roundup leads with the METR report on AI R&D acceleration — timelines are updating toward recursive self-improvement in 2027, but he warns against treating predictions as assurances; also covers Claude Fable 5.2, GPT-6 Cyber's kernel exploits, and the Jensen Huang scandal.

item.title: Terry Tao: Lean Grimoire
item.description: Tao rebuilt his interactive logic textbook as a crafting game with a coding agent — it now shows a live Lean proof of your game state, plus a fantasy mode where theorems become potions; he's asking for playtesters.

item.title: Cory Doctorow: Uber's labor crash
item.description: Uber's driver supply is finally cracking after years of sub-minimum pay, and Doctorow argues robotaxis can't save the model — replacing drivers who supply their own cars with $200k robots the company must own and maintain is worse economics, not better.

item.title: Bruce Schneier: Another Way Police Are Locating People from Their Smartphones
item.description: Penlink's Webloc builds a year-long, near-real-time picture of a phone's movements from location data harvested via weather, gaming, email and religious apps — and sells it to police, who can pull up every phone present at a place and time.

item.title: Bruce Schneier: Three People Arrested for AI-Enhanced Impersonation Fraud
item.description: Three men allegedly used AI to impersonate executives and lawyers and steal over $129m — Schneier's framing: this is security *from* AI, the third branch of AI security alongside security of and with AI.
